 Early voting surges in several states with competitive Senate races
 BY 
 Angi Gonzalez
 Nationwide 
 PUBLISHED 1:23 PM ET Oct. 22, 2026 
 PUBLISHED October 22, 2026 @1:23 PM 
 SHARE 
 A new analysis of early voting numbers shows participation surging in several states with competitive Senate races on Nov. 3.
 More than 16 million people across 41 states and the District of Columbia have already voted in the upcoming midterm elections. Data compiled by the Election Lab at the University of Florida says more than 10 million were cast using mail-in ballots and another 6 million through early in-person voting.
 Early voting totals were at around 13 million on Tuesday, a more than 40% increase over the same period during the 2022 midterms. The Associated Press found huge surges in Kansas and Texas, with Maine, North Carolina and Ohio also showing at least a 30% increase in early voting this year compared with four years ago. In each of these states, Democrats are trying to flip Republican-held Senate seats.
 “The midterms are a chance for people to go to the polls and say, ‘I have had enough,’” said Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass.
 But the data also shows not every hotly contested Senate race is driving voters to the polls just yet. In Georgia and Michigan, early voting totals are, for now, similar to those during the last midterms. Both races include seats currently held by Democrats.
 In Detroit on Wednesday night, Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers went head to head in what could be their last debate before Election Day. After a highly contentious debate between the two earlier this month, both candidates tried to focus on policy issues such as the economy.
 “The cost of gas, the cost of groceries, it all really goes back to this war in Iran,” El-Sayed said.
 Rogers argued gas prices would be much worse had the U.S. not launched the war with Iran.
 “You want to pay $8 a gallon of gas? Let Iran get a nuclear weapon,” Rogers said.
 Rogers and several other Republicans have sought to distance themselves from some of President Donald Trump’s policies this election cycle, but the former congressman did praise the administration for its immigration enforcement efforts.
